resources.string: Chat with everyone around you,\neven when there\'s no signal.
Messages hop phone to phone over Bluetooth and WiFi — no signal, no internet, no account.
Let Hopline find phones near you
Hopline links to your friends\' phones directly over Bluetooth and WiFi. Android calls this the “Nearby devices” permission.\n\nNothing leaves your group — there is no server.
Hopline can\'t find other phones without this. Please open Settings and allow Nearby devices.
This phone doesn\'t have Google Play services, which Hopline uses to link phones. Sorry — it won\'t work here.
For a trek, a camp, a festival — you\'ll get a 3-word code your friends type in
Type the 3 words your friend shows you, or scan their QR
three words, like: tiger river lamp
That doesn\'t look right — the code is three words.
Friends: open Hopline → Join a group → type these three words, or scan this.
Join my group “%1$s” on Hopline — offline group chat, no signal needed. Open Hopline → Join a group → type: %2$s
Hopline links to one group at a time. Tap a paused group to switch — its messages are kept.
Your phone will leave the radio of the current group and start finding this one. Nothing is deleted.
Share the group code so friends can join. Phones find each other on their own — no hotspot, no pairing.
Shrunk to travel the mesh (about 0.3 MB)
Up to 2 MB — big files hop slowly
That file is %1$s. Hopline can carry up to 2 MB — a smaller file or a photo works better on the mesh.
%1$s is a big file for the mesh — it may take several minutes to reach everyone. Send it?
Photos and files are off in very large groups — they would drown the radios everyone shares.
Nobody in range right now. Messages you send will be delivered when a phone comes close.
Nobody here yet. Ask a friend to open Hopline and join with your code — phones find each other on their own.
%1$s is out of range. Your message will be held and delivered when any phone reaches them.
Nobody has joined yet. Show them the group code!
One bar of signal helps the whole group
When anyone in the group gets internet, everyone can use a little of it. Requests hop to their phone; the answer hops back to the group chat.
Nobody has internet right now. You can still ask — it will happen the moment someone does.
Your phone has internet. Requests from the group run here.
%1$s\'s phone has internet right now. Requests go there.
Send an SMS or email home
Through the phone that has signal
Fetched as plain text to save data
Nobody has internet right now — your request is saved and will run as soon as someone does.
It travels through a friend\'s phone, and the whole group can see it — like handing a postcard down the line.
Nothing yet. Answers also appear in the group chat so everyone can read them.
Share my internet when I have signal
Friends can send short messages out and read web pages through your phone. It only ever uses a few KB.
Leave “%1$s”? Its messages and photos on this phone will be deleted.

Phones in your group link to each other directly over Bluetooth and WiFi — no tower, no router, no internet.

Every message is signed with your group's code and passed from phone to phone, so it can travel down a line of hikers or across a crowd, far beyond one phone's range.

Every phone keeps the group's messages for 48 hours and fills in anyone who was away. Walk off, come back — the chat catches up on its own.

The ticks never lie: ◷ waiting for a phone in range, ✓ on its way, ✓✓ phones confirmed. Tap your own message to see exactly who has it.

Anyone with the 3-word code can read the group, so treat it like a walkie-talkie, not a vault.
Free and open source — made for ForPublicOrg
Waiting — no phone in range has taken this yet. It keeps trying on its own.
Your phone has signal, so Hopline will open your messaging app with this filled in. Just tap send, then come back and tap “I sent it”.
Bluetooth is off — tap to turn it on
WiFi is off — tap to turn it on (it doesn\'t need a network)
Hopline needs the camera permission to take a photo. You can still attach one from your gallery.
